reasoning: The package is a standard binary repackaging (-bin) of DingTalk. The PKGBUILD downloads pre-built .deb archives from official Alibaba domains and pins them with SHA-512 checksums, preventing upstream swap attacks. The build and package functions perform standard extraction, file relocation, and library cleanup without executing fetched content or contacting unauthorized hosts. The disagreements in the reports were caused by transient API and parsing errors in the Qwen and Openrouter models, not by actual security concerns.
disagreement_analysis: The 'inconclusive' verdicts from Qwen and Openrouter were triggered by tool errors (HTTP 400 on PKGBUILD for Qwen, and a parsing failure on Makefile for Openrouter). Deepseek successfully audited all files and correctly identified the standard, safe packaging patterns. The advisory report from Openrouter also confirmed the PKGBUILD was safe before its Makefile parsing failed.
coverage_issues: Qwen model failed to audit PKGBUILD due to an HTTP 400 API error.
Openrouter model failed to audit Makefile due to a response parsing error.
All models skipped com.alibabainc.dingtalk.svg, incorrectly classifying it as a binary file (SVG is XML text), though this poses no AUR injection risk.
learnings: Implement retry logic or fallback models for transient API errors (e.g., HTTP 400) to prevent a single file failure from rendering the entire package audit inconclusive.
Improve file type detection to correctly identify SVG files as text/XML rather than skipping them as binaries, ensuring complete file coverage.
